decision.title: The owner's decisions of 2026-10-28: Schematron, source locations, the CLI's step limit
decision.summary: The owner fixes Schematron's edition, query bindings, outputs and exit status, makes source locations of parsed documents a processor setting AUTOMATIC, ALWAYS or NEVER, and removes the CLI's step limit.

body.p: by the orchestrator, from the owner's answers to the open points of packet and of the "Source locations for parsed input documents" item that was under "## Proposed" (moved here).

item.p: The edition is ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025 (4th edition, with group, library and rules, and the XSLT 3.1 and XQuery 3.1 binding); older schemas are read as the 4th edition reads them.

Query bindings: xslt, xslt2, xslt3, xslt4 and xpath, xpath2, xpath3, xpath31, xpath4 are accepted. A schema without queryBinding, and xslt, xpath and the reserved xslt4 and xpath4, are read as XSLT 4.0 and XPath 4.0, the versions sxml implements (, points B and 2a; as first recorded on 2026-10-28, a missing attribute was read as xslt3, never as XSLT 1.0, whose stylesheets sxml refuses with XTDE0160). xquery3 is rejected in one place with the error the standard gives.
Outputs: text and --format=json as for XSD, and --format=svrl.
Exit status 1 for a failed assert or a fired report whose role or flag is fatal or error, or that has neither; findings with other roles (warning, info) are printed and leave the status 0.
--schema with --schematron: XSD validation first, then the Schematron rules over the typed result; both reported, also when XSD validation fails.
SchXslt 1.10.1 (MIT) is vendored in third_party/ as the reference of a differential test only; nothing of it ships.

body.p: Source locations for parsed input documents (the owner's direction: optional, and on by default where it matters):

item.p: A processor setting with three values, AUTOMATIC (the zero value), ALWAYS, NEVER, for the documents sxml parses: by sxml_processor_parse_document, fn:doc, fn:parse-xml, fn:collection.

Under AUTOMATIC a document that a host parses before any program is compiled keeps its locations. Where sxml parses on a program's behalf, the compiled program decides: locations are kept when it calls fn:location, can reach functions dynamically (fn:function-lookup, fn:load-xquery-module, fn:transform, xsl:evaluate), or is a Schematron or XSD validation. xpath and xquery in the sxml command compile before they parse --context-item.
A dynamic error that names an input node prints its line and column when the node's document kept its locations.
--locations=always|never|automatic in the sxml command; the same three values in the JavaScript package.

Cost measured: 32 bytes a node; a 26 MB document of about 2.5 million nodes, release build, x86_64 Xeon 2.1 GHz: peak memory 171 MB without, 248 MB with (+45 %), time 3.0–3.2 s against 3.2–3.3 s. Streamed input builds no tree and pays nothing. Packet .

body.p: The sxml command's step limit (9): the sxml command sets no evaluation step limit; a long run is stopped by the person running it. The library's default (, ) stays for embedders and the JavaScript package; the conformance drivers keep their own bounds (, ). Packet .
SchXslt upstream (10): the sort-once fix for schxslt:replace-params is not offered upstream.
